sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putreṇa sāmātyena janārdana yathā ca saṃjayo rājñā mantraṃ rahasi śrāvitaḥ
english: O Janārdana, how the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, together with his ministers, had Sañjaya convey the king's secret counsel to you privately —

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhireṇa dāśārha tac cāpi viditaṃ tava yathoktaḥ saṃjayaś caiva tac ca sarvaṃ śrutaṃ tvayā
english: O descendant of Daśārha, that too is known to you — what Sañjaya was instructed to say, and all of it has been heard by you.

sanskrit: pañca nas tāta dīyantāṃ grāmā iti mahādyute kuśasthalaṃ vṛkasthalam āsandī vāraṇāvatam
english: "Let five villages be given to us" — so it was said, O greatly resplendent one: Kuśasthala, Vṛkasthala, Āsandi, and Vāraṇāvata,

sanskrit: avasānaṃ mahābāho kiṃ cid eva tu pañcamam iti duryodhano vācyaḥ suhṛdaś cāsya keśava
english: and any fifth place as the last, O mighty-armed one. Thus Duryodhana and his allies are to be addressed, O Keśava.

sanskrit: tac cāpi nākarod vākyaṃ śrutvā kṛṣṇa suyodhanaḥ yudhiṣṭhirasya dāśārha hrīmataḥ saṃdhim icchataḥ
english: Yet even upon hearing that appeal, O Kṛṣṇa, Suyodhana did not act upon it — the appeal of Yudhiṣṭhira, O descendant of Daśārha, that modest one who desires peace.

sanskrit: apradānena rājyasya yadi kṛṣṇa suyodhanaḥ saṃdhim icchen na kartavyas tatra gatvā kathaṃ cana
english: If Suyodhana should desire peace without restoring the kingdom, O Kṛṣṇa, then on no account should any peace be made upon going there.

sanskrit: śakṣyanti hi mahābāho pāṇḍavāḥ sṛñjayaiḥ saha dhārtarāṣṭrabalaṃ ghoraṃ kruddhaṃ pratisamāsitum
english: For the Pāṇḍavas together with the Sṛñjayas are capable, O mighty-armed one, of facing the terrible and wrathful army of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son.

sanskrit: na hi sāmnā na dānena śakyo 'rthas teṣu kaś cana tasmāt teṣu na kartavyā kṛpā te madhusūdana
english: For no purpose whatsoever can be achieved among them through conciliation or gifts; therefore no mercy should be shown toward them by you, O Madhusūdana.

sanskrit: sāmnā dānena vā kṛṣṇa ye na śāmyanti śatravaḥ moktavyas teṣu daṇḍaḥ syāj jīvitaṃ parirakṣatā
english: O Kṛṣṇa, enemies who are not pacified by conciliation or by gifts — the rod of punishment must be unleashed upon them by one who wishes to preserve his life.

sanskrit: tasmāt teṣu mahādaṇḍaḥ kṣeptavyaḥ kṣipram acyuta tvayā caiva mahābāho pāṇḍavaiḥ saha sṛñjayaiḥ
english: Therefore a great punishment must be swiftly meted out upon them, O Acyuta, by you yourself, O mighty-armed one, together with the Pāṇḍavas and the Sṛñjayas.

sanskrit: etat samarthaṃ pārthānāṃ tava caiva yaśaskaram kriyamāṇaṃ bhavet kṛṣṇa kṣatrasya ca sukhāvaham
english: This course of action is befitting the sons of Pṛthā and brings glory to you as well, O Kṛṣṇa; when carried out, it will bring happiness to the kṣatriya order.

sanskrit: kṣatriyeṇa hi hantavyaḥ kṣatriyo lobham āsthitaḥ akṣatriyo vā dāśārha svadharmam anutiṣṭhatā
english: For a kṣatriya overcome by greed must be slain by a kṣatriya — or even by a non-kṣatriya, O descendant of Daśārha, when he is upholding his own dharma.

sanskrit: anyatra brāhmaṇāt tāta sarvapāpeṣv avasthitāt gurur hi sarvavarṇānāṃ brāhmaṇaḥ prasṛtāgrabhuk
english: Excepting the brahmin, dear one, even one steeped in all sins — for the brahmin is the guru of all castes, the one who receives the first share of offerings.

sanskrit: yathāvadhye bhaved doṣo vadhyamāne janārdana sa vadhyasyāvadhe dṛṣṭa iti dharmavido viduḥ
english: Just as there is fault in slaying the undeserving, O Janārdana, that same fault is seen in sparing one who deserves to be slain — so those who know dharma declare.

sanskrit: yathā tvāṃ na spṛśed eṣa doṣaḥ kṛṣṇa tathā kuru pāṇḍavaiḥ saha dāśārha sṛñjayaiś ca sasainikaiḥ
english: Act in such a way that this fault does not touch you, O Kṛṣṇa, O descendant of Daśārha — together with the Pāṇḍavas and the Sṛñjayas and their forces.

sanskrit: punar uktaṃ ca vakṣyāmi viśrambheṇa janārdana kā nu sīmantinī mādṛk pṛthivyām asti keśava
english: And again I shall speak with confidence, O Janārdana: what woman like me exists upon this earth, O Keśava?

sanskrit: sutā drupadarājasya vedimadhyāt samutthitā dhṛṣṭadyumnasya bhaginī tava kṛṣṇa priyā sakhī
english: I am the daughter of King Drupada, risen from the midst of the sacrificial altar, the sister of Dhṛṣṭadyumna, your dear friend, O Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: ājamīḍhakulaṃ prāptā snuṣā pāṇḍor mahātmanaḥ mahiṣī pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ pañcendrasamavarcasām
english: I entered the lineage of Ājamīḍha; I am the daughter-in-law of the great-souled Pāṇḍu; I am the queen of the sons of Pāṇḍu, who are equal in splendour to the five Indras.

sanskrit: sutā me pañcabhir vīraiḥ pañca jātā mahārathāḥ abhimanyur yathā kṛṣṇa tathā te tava dharmataḥ
english: By five heroes five sons were born to me — great warriors all; and as Abhimanyu is to you, O Kṛṣṇa, so are they yours in point of dharma.

sanskrit: sāhaṃ keśagrahaṃ prāptā parikliṣṭā sabhāṃ gatā paśyatāṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ tvayi jīvati keśava
english: I — I suffered the seizing of my hair and, afflicted, was dragged into the assembly hall, while the sons of Pāṇḍu looked on, O Keśava, even while you lived.

sanskrit: jīvatsu kauraveyeṣu pāñcāleṣv atha vṛṣṇiṣu dāsībhūtāsmi pāpānāṃ sabhāmadhye vyavasthitā
english: While the Kurus, the Pāñcālas, and the Vṛṣṇis all still lived, I was made a slave by sinners and placed in the midst of the assembly.

sanskrit: nirāmarṣeṣv aceṣṭeṣu prekṣamāṇeṣu pāṇḍuṣu trāhi mām iti govinda manasā kāṅkṣito 'si me
english: While the sons of Pāṇḍu stood by without anger, without action, merely watching, I cried out in my heart: "Save me, O Govinda" — it was you I longed for.

sanskrit: yatra māṃ bhagavān rājā śvaśuro vākyam abravīt varaṃ vṛṇīṣva pāñcāli varārhāsi matāsi me
english: Then my father-in-law, the venerable king, spoke these words to me: "Choose a boon, O Pāñcālī — you are worthy of boons, so I regard you."

sanskrit: adāsāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ santu sarathāḥ sāyudhā iti mayokte yatra nirmuktā vanavāsāya keśava
english: When I said, "Let the Pāṇḍavas be free from slavery, with their chariots and weapons," they were released — only to be sent to forest exile, O Keśava.

sanskrit: evaṃvidhānāṃ duḥkhānām abhijño 'si janārdana trāhi māṃ puṇḍarīkākṣa sabhartṛjñātibāndhavām
english: You are acquainted with all such sufferings of mine, O Janārdana. Save me, O lotus-eyed one — together with my husbands, my kinsmen, and my relations.

sanskrit: nanv ahaṃ kṛṣṇa bhīṣmasya dhṛtarāṣṭrasya cobhayoḥ snuṣā bhavāmi dharmeṇa sāhaṃ dāsīkṛtābhavam
english: Am I not, O Kṛṣṇa, the rightful daughter-in-law of both Bhīṣma and Dhṛtarāṣṭra? And yet I was made a slave.

sanskrit: dhig balaṃ bhīmasenasya dhik pārthasya dhanuṣmatām yatra duryodhanaḥ kṛṣṇa muhūrtam api jīvati
english: Shame on the strength of Bhīmasena! Shame on the archery of the son of Pṛthā! That Duryodhana still lives even for a moment, O Kṛṣṇa!

sanskrit: yadi te 'ham anugrāhyā yadi te 'sti kṛpā mayi dhārtarāṣṭreṣu vai kopaḥ sarvaḥ kṛṣṇa vidhīyatām
english: If I am worthy of your grace, if you have compassion for me, then let all your wrath, O Kṛṣṇa, be directed against the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: ity uktvā mṛdusaṃhāraṃ vṛjināgraṃ sudarśanam sunīlam asitāpāṅgī puṇyagandhādhivāsitam
english: Having spoken thus, the dark-cornered-eyed one took in her left hand her tress of hair — gently bunched together, beautiful to behold at its tip, deep blue in hue, fragrant with sacred perfume —

sanskrit: sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpannaṃ mahābhujagavarcasam keśapakṣaṃ varārohā gṛhya savyena pāṇinā
english: endowed with every auspicious mark, radiant as a great serpent — that mass of hair, she the beautiful-hipped one held it in her left hand,

sanskrit: padmākṣī puṇḍarīkākṣam upetya gajagāminī aśrupūrṇekṣaṇā kṛṣṇā kṛṣṇaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: and approaching the lotus-eyed one, she who walks like an elephant and whose eyes were filled with tears — Kṛṣṇā spoke these words to Kṛṣṇa:

sanskrit: ayaṃ te puṇḍarīkākṣa duḥśāsanakaroddhṛtaḥ smartavyaḥ sarvakāleṣu pareṣāṃ saṃdhim icchatā
english: "This, O lotus-eyed one, was seized by Duḥśāsana's hand — it must be remembered at all times by you who desire peace with the enemy."

sanskrit: yadi bhīmārjunau kṛṣṇa kṛpaṇau saṃdhikāmukau pitā me yotsyate vṛddhaḥ saha putrair mahārathaiḥ
english: "If Bhīma and Arjuna are wretched and eager for peace, O Kṛṣṇa, my aged father will fight along with his sons, those great warriors."

sanskrit: pañca caiva mahāvīryāḥ putrā me madhusūdana abhimanyuṃ puraskṛtya yotsyanti kurubhiḥ saha
english: "And my five sons of great valour, O Madhusūdana, with Abhimanyu at their head, will fight against the Kurus."

sanskrit: duḥśāsanabhujaṃ śyāmaṃ saṃchinnaṃ pāṃsuguṇṭhitam yady ahaṃ taṃ na paśyāmi kā śāntir hṛdayasya me
english: "If I do not see Duḥśāsana's dark arm severed and rolled in the dust, what peace can there be for my heart?"

sanskrit: trayodaśa hi varṣāṇi pratīkṣantyā gatāni me nidhāya hṛdaye manyuṃ pradīptam iva pāvakam
english: "Thirteen years have passed for me while I waited, carrying in my heart a fury blazing like fire."

sanskrit: vidīryate me hṛdayaṃ bhīmavākśalyapīḍitam yo 'yam adya mahābāhur dharmaṃ samanupaśyati
english: "My heart is being torn apart, pierced by the arrow of Bhīma's words — he who, mighty-armed as he is, today looks to dharma alone."

sanskrit: ity uktvā bāṣpasannena kaṇṭhenāyatalocanā ruroda kṛṣṇā sotkampaṃ sasvaraṃ bāṣpagadgadam
english: Having spoken thus, Kṛṣṇā, she of the wide eyes, wept with a voice choked with tears — trembling, with a voice broken by sobs.

sanskrit: stanau pīnāyataśroṇī sahitāv abhivarṣatī dravībhūtam ivātyuṣṇam utsṛjad vāri netrajam
english: She of the full breasts and rounded hips, her two breasts drenched together, shed tears from her eyes as if releasing water made burning hot and melted.

sanskrit: tām uvāca mahābāhuḥ keśavaḥ parisāntvayan acirād drakṣyase kṛṣṇe rudatīr bharatastriyaḥ
english: The mighty-armed Keśava spoke to her, consoling her: "O Kṛṣṇā, before long you shall see the women of the Bhārata line weeping."

sanskrit: evaṃ tā bhīru rotsyanti nihatajñātibāndhavāḥ hatamitrā hatabalā yeṣāṃ kruddhāsi bhāmini
english: "Thus, O timid one, O passionate lady, they shall weep — those whose kinsmen and relatives have been slain, whose allies are slain, whose armies are destroyed — they at whom your wrath is directed."

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca tat kariṣyāmi bhīmārjunayamaiḥ saha yudhiṣṭhiraniyogena daivāc ca vidhinirmitāt
english: "And I shall bring this about, together with Bhīma, Arjuna, and the twins, by the command of Yudhiṣṭhira and by the ordinance fashioned by destiny."

sanskrit: dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ kālapakvā na cec chṛṇvanti me vacaḥ śeṣyante nihatā bhūmau śvaśṛgālādanīkṛtāḥ
english: "If the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, ripened by Time, do not heed my words, they shall lie slain upon the earth, made food for jackals and dogs."

sanskrit: caled dhi himavāñ śailo medinī śatadhā bhavet dyauḥ patec ca sanakṣatrā na me moghaṃ vaco bhavet
english: "Though the Himālaya mountain may tremble, though the earth may shatter into a hundred pieces, though the sky may fall with all its stars — my words shall not be in vain."

sanskrit: satyaṃ te pratijānāmi kṛṣṇe bāṣpo nigṛhyatām hatāmitrāñ śriyā yuktān acirād drakṣyase patīn
english: "I swear this truth to you, O Kṛṣṇā — restrain your tears. Before long you shall see your husbands, adorned with glory, their enemies slain."

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca kurūṇām adya sarveṣāṃ bhavān suhṛd anuttamaḥ saṃbandhī dayito nityam ubhayoḥ pakṣayor api
english: Arjuna said: You are today the best of friends to all the Kurus, a beloved kinsman always, on both sides alike.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavair dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ pratipādyam anāmayam samarthaḥ praśamaṃ caiṣāṃ kartuṃ tvam asi keśava
english: You are capable, O Keśava, of bringing about the well-being that must be secured between the Pāṇḍavas and the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and of bringing peace to them.

sanskrit: tvam itaḥ puṇḍarīkākṣa suyodhanam amarṣaṇam śāntyarthaṃ bhārataṃ brūyā yat tad vācyam amitrahan
english: From here, O lotus-eyed one, O slayer of enemies, you could speak to wrathful Suyodhana whatever must be said for the sake of peace among the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tvayā dharmārthayuktaṃ ced uktaṃ śivam anāmayam hitaṃ nādāsyate bālo diṣṭasya vaśam eṣyati
english: If what is spoken by you — auspicious, wholesome, grounded in dharma and artha — is not accepted by that fool, then he will fall under the power of fate.

sanskrit: bhagavān uvāca dharmyam asmaddhitaṃ caiva kurūṇāṃ yad anāmayam eṣa yāsyāmi rājānaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭram abhīpsayā
english: The Blessed One said: That which is righteous, beneficial to us, and conducive to the well-being of the Kurus — I shall go to King Dhṛtarāṣṭra with that intent.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato vyapete tamasi sūrye vimala udgate maitre muhūrte saṃprāpte mṛdvarciṣi divākare
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, when the darkness had departed, when the pure sun had risen, when the auspicious hour of Mitra had arrived, when the sun shone with gentle rays,

sanskrit: kaumude māsi revatyāṃ śaradante himāgame sphītasasyasukhe kāle kalyaḥ sattvavatāṃ varaḥ
english: in the month of Kaumuda, under the asterism Revatī, at the end of autumn when winter was setting in, in the pleasant season of abundant crops — the best of the vigorous ones arose hale.

sanskrit: maṅgalyāḥ puṇyanirghoṣā vācaḥ śṛṇvaṃś ca sūnṛtāḥ brāhmaṇānāṃ pratītānām ṛṣīṇām iva vāsavaḥ
english: Hearing the auspicious, holy, and agreeable words of confident brahmins — like Vāsava hearing the words of the seers —

sanskrit: kṛtvā paurvāhṇikaṃ kṛtyaṃ snātaḥ śucir alaṃkṛtaḥ upatasthe vivasvantaṃ pāvakaṃ ca janārdanaḥ
english: having performed the morning rites, bathed, purified, and adorned, Janārdana worshipped the sun Vivasvān and fire.

sanskrit: ṛṣabhaṃ pṛṣṭha ālabhya brāhmaṇān abhivādya ca agniṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā paśyan kalyāṇam agrataḥ
english: Having stroked a bull on its back, having saluted the brahmins, having circumambulated the sacred fire, seeing auspiciousness before him,

sanskrit: tat pratijñāya vacanaṃ pāṇḍavasya janārdanaḥ śiner naptāram āsīnam abhyabhāṣata sātyakim
english: Janārdana, having pledged that word of the Pāṇḍava, spoke to Sātyaki, the grandson of Śini, who was seated there.

sanskrit: ratha āropyatāṃ śaṅkhaś cakraṃ ca gadayā saha upāsaṅgāś ca śaktyaś ca sarvapraharaṇāni ca
english: "Let the conch, the discus, and the mace be placed on the chariot, along with the quivers, the lances, and all the weapons."

sanskrit: duryodhano hi duṣṭātmā karṇaś ca sahasaubalaḥ na ca śatrur avajñeyaḥ prākṛto 'pi balīyasā
english: "For Duryodhana is of wicked soul, and so is Karṇa together with Śakuni's son; and an enemy, however ordinary, must not be treated with contempt even by the powerful."

sanskrit: tatas tan matam ājñāya keśavasya puraḥsarāḥ prasasrur yojayiṣyanto rathaṃ cakragadābhṛtaḥ
english: Then, having understood the intent of Keśava, his forerunners went forth to harness the chariot of him who bears the discus and the mace.

sanskrit: taṃ dīptam iva kālāgnim ākāśagam ivādhvagam candrasūryaprakāśābhyāṃ cakrābhyāṃ samalaṃkṛtam
english: That chariot — blazing like the fire of dissolution, like a traveller moving through the sky — was adorned with two wheels that shone with the brilliance of the moon and the sun,

sanskrit: ardhacandraiś ca candraiś ca matsyaiḥ samṛgapakṣibhiḥ puṣpaiś ca vividhaiś citraṃ maṇiratnaiś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: decorated with half-moons and full moons, with fish, with deer and birds, with flowers of various kinds, and on all sides with gems and jewels — a wondrous sight.

sanskrit: taruṇādityasaṃkāśaṃ bṛhantaṃ cārudarśanam maṇihemavicitrāṅgaṃ sudhvajaṃ supatākinam
english: Resembling the newly risen sun, vast, and beautiful to behold, with body parts wrought from gems and gold, with a fine standard and fine pennants —

sanskrit: sūpaskaram anādhṛṣyaṃ vaiyāghraparivāraṇam yaśoghnaṃ pratyamitrāṇāṃ yadūnāṃ nandivardhanam
english: well-equipped, invincible, draped with tiger skins — the destroyer of the glory of enemies and the increaser of joy among the Yadus —

sanskrit: vājibhiḥ sainyasugrīvameghapuṣpabalāhakaiḥ snātaiḥ saṃpādayāṃ cakruḥ saṃpannaiḥ sarvasaṃpadā
english: they harnessed it with the horses Sainya, Sugrīva, Meghapuṣpa, and Balāhaka — bathed and endowed with every excellence.

sanskrit: mahimānaṃ tu kṛṣṇasya bhūya evābhivardhayan sughoṣaḥ patagendreṇa dhvajena yuyuje rathaḥ
english: Further magnifying the greatness of Kṛṣṇa, the chariot was yoked with the banner Sughoṣa bearing the king of birds.

sanskrit: taṃ meruśikharaprakhyaṃ meghadundubhinisvanam āruroha rathaṃ śaurir vimānam iva puṇyakṛt
english: That chariot, resembling the peak of Mount Meru, rumbling like the thundering drums of storm clouds, was mounted by the hero Śauri as if it were a divine vehicle by one who has earned merit.

sanskrit: tataḥ sātyakim āropya prayayau puruṣottamaḥ pṛthivīṃ cāntarikṣaṃ ca rathaghoṣeṇa nādayan
english: Then, having taken Sātyaki up with him, the Best of Men set forth, making both the earth and the sky resound with the roar of the chariot.

sanskrit: vyapoḍhābhraghanaḥ kālaḥ kṣaṇena samapadyata śivaś cānuvavau vāyuḥ praśāntam abhavad rajaḥ
english: In a moment the sky became clear of dense clouds; a gentle wind blew in his wake; the dust settled.

sanskrit: pradakṣiṇānulomāś ca maṅgalyā mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ prayāṇe vāsudevasya babhūvur anuyāyinaḥ
english: At the departure of Vāsudeva, auspicious beasts and birds moving clockwise and in the right direction followed in his train.

sanskrit: maṅgalyārthapadaiḥ śabdair anvavartanta sarvaśaḥ sārasāḥ śatapatrāś ca haṃsāś ca madhusūdanam
english: Cranes, lotuses, and swans followed Madhusūdana on every side with cries full of auspicious import and meaning.

sanskrit: mantrāhutimahāhomair hūyamānaś ca pāvakaḥ pradakṣiṇaśikho bhūtvā vidhūmaḥ samapadyata
english: And the sacred fire, being fed with great oblations of mantras and offerings, became smokeless and turned its flame clockwise.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭho vāmadevaś ca bhūridyumno gayaḥ krathaḥ śukranāradavālmīkā marutaḥ kuśiko bhṛguḥ
english: Vasiṣṭha, Vāmadeva, Bhūridyumna, Gaya, Krātha, Śukra, Nārada, Vālmīki, the Maruts, Kuśika, and Bhṛgu —

sanskrit: brahmadevarṣayaś caiva kṛṣṇaṃ yadusukhāvaham pradakṣiṇam avartanta sahitā vāsavānujam
english: together with the divine seers and brahmic sages, they all circled clockwise around Kṛṣṇa, the younger brother of Vāsava, the bringer of joy to the Yadus.

sanskrit: evam etair mahābhāgair maharṣigaṇasādhubhiḥ pūjitaḥ prayayau kṛṣṇaḥ kurūṇāṃ sadanaṃ prati
english: Thus honoured by these greatly blessed and virtuous hosts of great seers, Kṛṣṇa set forth toward the abode of the Kurus.

sanskrit: taṃ prayāntam anuprāyāt kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ bhīmasenārjunau cobhau mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau
english: As he set forth, Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Kuntī followed him, and both Bhīmasena and Arjuna, and the two Pāṇḍava sons of Mādrī.

sanskrit: cekitānaś ca vikrānto dhṛṣṭaketuś ca cedipaḥ drupadaḥ kāśirājaś ca śikhaṇḍī ca mahārathaḥ
english: The valiant Cekitāna, Dhṛṣṭaketu the king of the Cedis, Drupada, the king of Kāśi, and the great warrior Śikhaṇḍī —

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ saputraś ca virāṭaḥ kekayaiḥ saha saṃsādhanārthaṃ prayayuḥ kṣatriyāḥ kṣatriyarṣabham
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna with his sons, Virāṭa together with the Kekayas — these warriors went forth to accompany that bull among warriors.

sanskrit: tato 'nuvrajya govindaṃ dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ rājñāṃ sakāśe dyutimān uvācedaṃ vacas tadā
english: Then the resplendent Dharmarāja Yudhiṣṭhira, following Govinda, spoke these words in the presence of the kings:

sanskrit: yo naiva kāmān na bhayān na lobhān nārthakāraṇāt anyāyam anuvarteta sthirabuddhir alolupaḥ
english: "He who, firm of mind and free from greed, does not follow unrighteousness out of desire, or fear, or greed, or for the sake of material gain —

sanskrit: dharmajño dhṛtimān prājñaḥ sarvabhūteṣu keśavaḥ īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ devadevaḥ pratāpavān
english: that knower of dharma, resolute, wise — Keśava, the lord of all beings in all creatures, god of gods, resplendent in might."
